clue.text: Keep learner in class

indicators.note: the learner is placed in the class, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a caste is a social class
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher is told to keep a pupil behind in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' reads as a verb about detention, but it is the noun: the stronghold of a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the central tower of a fortified stronghold, so the two words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Set up mine in the arena

parts.note: to cock a gun is to set it up ready for firing
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a mine in the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit was the arena where cockfights were held, and by extension any place of conflict.

clue.text: Military cap is used: it's a knockout

parts.note: SH is short for second-hand, meaning used
KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout

explanation.surface: A second-hand army hat is described as stunning.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall peaked military hat with a plume, worn by soldiers in the 19th century.

clue.text: Inspect small instrument and be quick about it

parts.note: to look at is to inspect
a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Someone is told to examine a little instrument and hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'look sharp' is a command to hurry up.

clue.text: A man's drink

definitions.meaning: in the board game ..., each playing piece is called a man
a swallow of liquid, or beer drawn from the cask

explanation.surface: A short remark about something a man drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is': a man is one thing, a drink the other. Draughts is the British name for the game of checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Each disc in checkers is a piece also called a man, and a single gulp of beer from the barrel is likewise a measure.

clue.text: Talk about sporting event on Sunday

indicators.note: in a down answer the event is placed on top of Sunday

parts.note: the discus is a throwing event in athletics

explanation.surface: People chat about a weekend sports fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss a matter is to talk it over, so the phrase is a direct synonym.

clue.text: A politician has one form of defence

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal politician
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A politician has a single way of defending himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea that the accused was elsewhere, a kind of legal defence.

clue.text: Drug tea? It excited a feeling of appreciation

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of drug tea it are mixed

explanation.surface: A spiked cup of tea leaves the drinker overwhelmed with thankfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratitude is thankfulness, the warm feeling of appreciating what someone did for you.

clue.text: Girl gets thanks when taking control

indicators.note: the thanks takes in the control, holding it inside

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
to be at the helm is to be in control

explanation.surface: A young woman is thanked once she is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a female first name, and crosswords treat any such name as a girl.

clue.text: Fabric for attorney's cloak

parts.note: DA is the American district attorney
to mask something is to cloak or hide it

explanation.surface: A lawyer's coat is made of some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven textile, such as silk or linen, so it is a fabric.

clue.text: Beef about rail chaos?

indicators.note: about here means all over the place, so the letters of rail chaos are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble about chaos on the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like a verb meaning complain, but it is the cattle. 'about' rearranges RAIL CHAOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Charolais is a French breed of cattle raised for its meat, so it is a type of beef.

clue.text: One gets the setter to adopt a good appearance

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the setter takes in the next pieces, so they go inside him

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Someone decides the crossword setter should adopt a tidier look.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is the public look or impression someone presents, a synonym for how they come across.

clue.text: Having second thoughts about obligation to be devout

indicators.note: the second thoughts go around the obligation, enclosing it

parts.note: a PS, or postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
an IOU is a written promise to repay a debt

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders a duty they owe and decides to be religious.
explanation.walkthrough: PS, the postscript at the end of a letter, stands for second thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious and devout are synonyms describing someone deeply religious.

clue.text: Metal or salt containing little uranium

indicators.note: the salt holds the next pieces within it

parts.note: alum is a double sulphate salt used in dyeing
mini means small
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A chemist describes a metal or salt with a trace of uranium in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium, the British spelling, is a light silvery chemical element classed as a metal.

clue.text: A small fastening can alter one's course

parts.note: a tin is a can
to tack is to change direction when sailing

explanation.surface: A tiny fastening has the power to change your path in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintack is a short tin-coated nail, a small fixing used by upholsterers.

clue.text: People mobbing a bishop in Reading

indicators.note: the people crowd around the bishop, surrounding him

parts.note: a nation is a people
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A crowd surrounds a bishop in the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the English town, but it is reading aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is a spoken account or recitation, like a reading of a story.

clue.text: Lavish old Bob with drink

parts.note: bob was slang for the old British shilling, abbreviated s
to lap up is to drink eagerly

explanation.surface: An old acquaintance called Bob is extravagant with alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a shilling in pre-1971 British money, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, generous one, an informal British idiom.

clue.text: Sleep in a container on a mountain

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits on top of the final a
the sleep goes inside the container phrase

parts.note: an urn is a container, with a becoming an
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps in a box on a mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapurna is a peak in the Himalayas of Nepal, one of the highest in the world.

clue.text: King is absorbed by subject's global line

indicators.note: the king is soaked up inside the subject, so it goes within it

parts.note: a topic is a subject
R is from Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is engrossed in a subject's world view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' suggests a royal subject, but it is a topic of discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude drawn around the globe.

clue.text: Situation in which bounder falls

indicators.note: the bounder is placed within the situation

parts.note: a case is a situation, as in that being the case
a cad is an ungentlemanly bounder

explanation.surface: A scene in which a scoundrel comes a cropper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' reads as a verb about the bounder, but it is the noun, a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a small waterfall, and falls is another word for a waterfall.

clue.text: Food for Bonfire Night?

definitions.meaning: loud fireworks set off on the fifth of November

explanation.surface: A question about what to eat on Bonfire Night.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonfire Night, 5 November in Britain, is marked with fireworks; sausages, also called by the same slang name, are a traditional food there.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang both for sausages and for noisy firecrackers.

clue.text: Groundwork used to catch fish — about a ton

indicators.note: the fish goes around the next pieces

parts.note: a bass is a fish
I is one, which means a
C is the Roman numeral 100, a ton

explanation.surface: A fisherman's foundations are used to land a heavy catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The basics are the fundamentals, the groundwork from which everything else is built.

clue.text: Reckoning to eat a bird — part of the breast

indicators.note: the reckoning swallows the bird, holding it inside

parts.note: a sum is a reckoning or calculation
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A sum is worked out before eating some poultry breast.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Bitterness over work and career

indicators.note: in a down answer the bitterness sits over the work

parts.note: gall is bitterness or resentment
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone resents the job and the professional life that goes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a profession, but it is the verb meaning rush along.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush headlong at speed, which a horse does when it gallops.

clue.text: Prophets of doom fabricated star's mail

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the letters of star's mail are reassembled

explanation.surface: Doom-mongers made up a celebrity's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: People who raise needless fears and predict disaster are prophets of doom, scaremongers.

clue.text: Note academic's position in the field

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
a don is a university academic

explanation.surface: A memo about a professor's standing in their discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-ON is a fielding position in cricket; 'field' suggests an academic discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-on is a cricket fielding place, near the bowler on the leg side.

clue.text: Ancient English gum

parts.note: past means bygone, of long ago

explanation.surface: An old English glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is an adhesive, and to gum something is to stick it, so both name glue.

clue.text: Pole's longing to be fashionable

parts.note: S is the South Pole
a wish is a longing

explanation.surface: A Polish person yearns to be stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland, but it is a magnetic pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British for smart and stylish.

clue.text: Many retreat before landowner

indicators.note: the retreat comes before the many, putting it first

parts.note: a lair is a hiding place or den
D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of people withdraw ahead of the landlord's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Agreement to one playing instrument

parts.note: accord means agreement
I is the Roman numeral one
a film or show that is on is playing

explanation.surface: A musician agrees to let someone play the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The accordion is a musical instrument with bellows and keys, an example of the class.

clue.text: Atonement for one captivated by money

indicators.note: the one is held captive inside the money

parts.note: pence are British coins
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: Someone seduced by wealth must make amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is an act of self-punishment done to make amends for sin, a synonym for atonement.

clue.text: Bedlam can appear on the border

parts.note: may means can, as in permission
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: Chaos may break out at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is the verb of permission, not a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam and mayhem are both synonyms for violent disorder and chaos.
